result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.load_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Calculate load centrality scores for all nodes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L18516-L18648){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.load_centrality( normalized=True, cutoff=None, attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Load centrality measures the fraction of shortest paths that pass through each node. It is similar to betweenness centrality but uses a different accumulation formula that counts the 'load' or traffic on nodes from shortest path routing. The key differences from betweenness centrality: - **Betweenness**: uses dependency accumulation with path count ratios - **Load**: uses simpler load counting based on predecessors Both metrics identify important bridge nodes, but load centrality can produce slightly different rankings that may be more intuitive for certain applications like network traffic analysis or identifying bottlenecks in routing systems. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [normalized]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), normalizes scores by dividing by `(n-1)(n-2)` where `n` is the number of nodes. If `False`, returns raw load counts. [cutoff]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional maximum path length to consider. Only paths of length ≤ cutoff are included. If `None` (default), considers all path lengths. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Column name to store load centrality scores in the node DataFrame. If `None` (default), automatically uses 'load_centrality'. Overwrites column if it already exists. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns a dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores in NDF and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to load centrality scores. If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Identify bridge nodes using load centrality: ::: {#7f8b49b9 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec # Create a network with a central bridge graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="Bridge") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "Bridge") .add_edge("Bridge", "C") .add_edge("C", "D") ) scores = graph.load_centrality(return_dict=True) bridge_id = graph.get_id_from_label("Bridge") # High load score for bridge node scores[bridge_id] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 0.6666666666666666 ``` ::: ::: Compare load vs betweenness centrality: ::: {#2c48f249 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("C", "D") ) load = graph.load_centrality(return_dict=True) betweenness = graph.betweenness_centrality(return_dict=True) # Compare load and betweenness for each node comparison = { graph.get_label_from_id(nid): (load[nid], betweenness[nid]) for nid in sorted(load.keys()) } # Returns dict mapping labels to (load, betweenness) tuples comparison ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {'A': (0.0, 0.0), 'B': (0.6666666666666666, 0.6666666666666666), 'C': (0.6666666666666666, 0.6666666666666666), 'D': (0.0, 0.0)} ``` ::: ::: Store centrality as node attribute for later use: ::: {#cf363e39 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() for i in range(5): graph.add_node(label=str(i)) for i in range(4): graph.add_edge(str(i), str(i+1)) graph.load_centrality(attr_name="load") graph.get_node_attrs("load") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` {3: 0.6666666666666666, 1: 0.0, 5: 0.0, 4: 0.5, 2: 0.5} ``` ::: :::
